rules.label: Medications that change heart rate
rules.text: A beta-blocker blunts the exercise heart rate: set intensity by effort (RPE) and the talk test, not a heart-rate zone.

rules.label: Warning sign during exercise
rules.text: Dizziness or unusual breathlessness: stop now and have him sit.

rules.label: Scope of practice
rules.text: Medication timing and doses are for his doctor.

The direction follows the source: a beta-blocker blunts the exercise heart rate (often by 10-40 beats per minute), so a heart-rate zone from an age formula overstates the effort he needs, and RPE or the talk test set intensity instead. brief.situation: You are a personal trainer. Walter Grant, 63 (a fictional client), has high blood pressure, is cleared by his doctor for moderate-intensity exercise and has a new fitness watch. Today is his first cardio session with you.
handover: The gym's emergency action plan: call 911, send the front desk to meet the crew, bring the AED.
Trainers set intensity and watch for warning signs; medications are for his doctor.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes.
The screen shows the client, your read-outs and findings, the plan and the rules that apply now.
When you end the session you write the record and explain your reasoning.

safetyNote: Teaching case for exam practice; fictional client. Not medical advice.

source.note: Three minutes at a near-maximal effort before he becomes lightheaded is the author's figure.
Four more minutes on the treadmill while lightheaded before he nearly falls is the author's figure.
Eight minutes for the ambulance is the author's figure; response times vary.

parts.label: Intensity
parts.criteria: Metoprolol, a beta-blocker, blunts the exercise heart rate, so an age-formula zone (and heart-rate reserve) overstates the effort; set intensity by RPE (about 4-6 of 10, moderate as cleared) and the talk test.
parts.modelAnswer: He takes metoprolol, which holds his heart rate down, so the watch's 110-126 zone would push him far past the moderate effort he is cleared for. I used effort, 4-6 out of 10, and the talk test.

parts.label: Warning signs
parts.criteria: Lightheadedness or unusual breathlessness during exercise: stop at once and sit him down; if it does not settle or he nearly faints, call 911.
parts.modelAnswer: If he becomes lightheaded or unusually breathless, the session stops and he sits; if he does not recover quickly or nearly faints, 911.

parts.label: Next time
parts.criteria: No advice about his medication timing or dose (his doctor's); report any symptom to his doctor; keep the effort-based method; record it.
parts.modelAnswer: His medication is his doctor's call, so I made no suggestion about it. Any symptom goes to his doctor with my notes, and we keep training by effort.

expertPath.text: Read the note and the medication list: metoprolol. Explain why the watch's zone does not fit; set intensity by effort 4-6 and the talk test.
When the watch buzzes 'below zone', keep him where he can talk in sentences; check his effort.
A full record; any symptom would go to his doctor; no advice on his medication.

rpeSession.headline: Intensity that fits his medication
rpeSession.body: A beta-blocker blunts the exercise heart rate, so a zone from the age formula would drive him past the moderate effort he is cleared for. Effort and the talk test fit.

stopped.headline: Stopped in time, but the zone was the mistake
stopped.body: Chasing a heart rate his medication holds down took him to an effort of 8 and made him lightheaded. You stopped at once; next time set intensity by effort.

gaps.headline: Done, with gaps
gaps.body: Check how intensity was set (effort, not a heart-rate formula, on a beta-blocker), and whether he knows why.

nearFaint.headline: A warning sign is a stop sign
nearFaint.body: Lightheadedness and breathlessness during exercise mean stop and sit him down now. Pushing on until he nearly fainted turned a warning into an emergency.

medAdvice.headline: Medication is his doctor's call
medAdvice.body: Moving or skipping a blood pressure medicine is a medical decision. Change the intensity method instead.

time_up.headline: No record
time_up.body: The session ended without a record.

scoring.modelReasoning: He takes metoprolol, a beta-blocker, which blunts the exercise heart rate (often by 10-40 beats a minute), so a zone from 220 minus age, or heart-rate reserve from his resting rate, overstates the effort he needs and pushes him past the moderate intensity he is cleared for. Set intensity by RPE (about 4-6 of 10) and the talk test, explain why, and ignore the watch's buzz. Lightheadedness or unusual breathlessness means stop at once; 911 if he nearly faints. Medication timing is his doctor's decision; report symptoms to the doctor and record the session.
